summary: Benoît Vermander works in sinology and religious studies. He studied at Sciences Po, Yale University, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director at Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) and became professor at Fudan University in 2009.

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied under Paul Demiéville and Seizan Yanagida, earning a Doctorat d'État from Paris Diderot University. He held posts at Cornell (~1983–1987), Stanford (~1987–2006), and Columbia University (~2006).

Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as director at the Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1979–1983) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).

Bernard Goldman was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1952–1955) and held a post at Wayne State University from circa 1956 to 1988.

Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). During his academic career, he held positions at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian and archaeologist. He held academic posts at the University of Oldenburg (~1987–1992) and the University of Heidelberg (~2003–2020).

Bernfried Schlerath specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Paul Thieme (~1950–1954) and held posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1958–1963), the University of Marburg (~1964–1974), and the Free University of Berlin (~1974–1992).
Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist. He succeeded Heinrich Lüders and held a post at the University of Berlin from circa 1937 to 1945.

Bernhard Forssman specializes in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and under Karl Hoffmann. He held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Leopold von Schroeder and Franz Kielhorn across several universities. His career included posts at the University of Vienna, the Tibetan-Iranian Institute/Asia Institute, and Columbia University.

Bernhard Hirzel was an Indologist who studied at the universities of Zurich, Göttingen, Berlin, and Paris, including study under Franz Bopp. He held teaching posts at the University of Zurich as reader (1833), Dozent (1835–1837), and Privatdozent (1845).

Bernhard Karlgren was a scholar in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala University (~1907–1915) and held posts at Uppsala University (~1915–1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist who completed degrees at Frankfurt and Cologne. He held positions at the University of Cologne (1966–1970, 1972–1976), the Nepal Research Centre (~1970–1972), Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman worked in Buddhist studies. He studied at Brooklyn Polytechnic, NYU, and UCLA, and trained under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He co-founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and founded Zen Peacemakers in 1980.

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her doctorate under Jonathan A. Silk. She has held posts at the University of Heidelberg (~2015) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Heymann Steinthal. He held posts at the University of Halle (1866, 1867–1870) and the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer specialized in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under August Conrady, Georg von der Gabelentz, and others. He held posts at AMNH, Columbia University, and the Field Museum (1907).

Bettina Bäumer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, having studied across Europe, earning a doctorate at Munich. She studied under Swami Lakshman Joo and held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Alice Boner Institute, University of Vienna, and IIAS.

Bettine Birge works in sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, where she studied under Wm. Theodore de Bary, and also studied under Masaaki Sugiyama. She was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Paul Deussen, Georg Simmel, Emil Sieg, and Eugen Hultzsch. She held posts at Kiel, Halle, Hamburg, the University of London (~1934–1945), Oxford (~1936–1944), and the University of Colombo (1945–1949).
